'''Ellen Elizabeth Kirkman''' is a professor of mathematics at [[Wake Forest University]]. Her research interests include [[noncommutative algebra]], [[representation theory]], and [[homological algebra]].<ref>[http://college.wfu.edu/math/people/faculty/kirkman Dr. Ellen Kirkman]</ref>

==Education==
She received her Ph.D. in Mathematics and M.A. in Statistics from [[Michigan State University]] in 1975.
Her doctoral dissertation, ''On the Characterization of Inertial Coefficient Rings'', was supervised by Edward C. Ingraham.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=15430|title=Ellen Kirkman}}</ref>

==Professional activities==
Kirkman is on the board of directors for [[Enhancing Diversity in Graduate Education]] (EDGE), a program dedicated to helping women pursuing studies in mathematical sciences. From 2012 to 2020, she served as treasurer of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] (AWM).<ref>[https://sites.google.com/site/awmmath/awm/history AWM History], retrieved 2014-12-31.</ref>

Kirkman's professional activities include serving on the [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS) Nominating Committee from 2009 to 11,<ref>{{cite web|title=AMS Committees|url=https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/nomcom-past.html|website=www.ams.org|publisher=American Mathematical Society|accessdate=19 August 2015}}</ref> as a [[Mathematical Association of America]] (MAA) Governor from 2006 to 2008, on the Joint Data Committee of AMS-ASA-MAA-IMS-SIAM (2000– 2007 and 2009–present)<ref>{{cite web|title=AMS Committees|url=https://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/comm-all.html|website=www.ams.org|publisher=American Mathematical Society|accessdate=19 August 2015}}</ref> and directing the CBMS 2010 survey of undergraduate mathematical sciences programs.<ref>{{cite web|title=The EDGE Program|url=http://www.edgeforwomen.org/edge-1999/|website=www.edgeforwomen.org|publisher=Sylvia Bozeman and Rhonda Hughes EDGE Founcation|accessdate=19 August 2015}}</ref> She is also an associate editor of Communications in Algebra.<ref>{{cite web|title=Editorial Board|url=http://www.tandfonline.com/action/journalInformation?show=editorialBoard&journalCode=lagb20|website=Communications in Algebra|publisher=Taylor and Francis|accessdate=19 August 2015}}</ref>

Kirkman served as treasurer and was on the Executive Committee of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] from 2012 to 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=History: AWM Officers|url=https://awm-math.org/about/history/|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|access-date=30 March 2021}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 2012, Kirkman became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]</ref> is also a fellow of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] inducted in 2019.<ref>{{citation|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/|title=2019 Class of AWM Fellows|publisher=[[Association for Women in Mathematics]]|accessdate=2019-01-26}}</ref>
Additionally, she received service awards from Wake Forest University and the Southeastern Section of the MAA. In 2022, she received the [[AWM Service Award]] "for her eight years of service (2012 – 2020) as AWM Treasurer and Chair of the Financial Oversight and Investment Committee, for her service on the Membership Portfolio Committee, and for her role as an organizer and a research leader in the WINART (Women in Noncommutative Algebra and Representation Theory) Research Network."<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 AWM service award |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-service-award/awm-service-award-2022/}}</ref>
